# Landlord insurance

Flat 3, 22 Cardigan Road. The buildings side is the freeholder's block policy (I pay through the service charge), so my own policy is landlord contents, liability and loss of rent. Policy with Alan Boswell, number **LND-62044**, renewal 1 Aug. Premium £312 a year.

## What the policy covers

- Landlord contents: £8,000 (carpets, curtains, white goods, the sofa bed, the wardrobe)
- Property owner's liability: £2m. If Marek trips on a loose stair rod in the flat, that's this
- Loss of rent: up to 12 months, max £12,000, only if the flat is uninhabitable due to an insured event
- Tenant default / rent guarantee: NOT included. Quote for it was £148 extra, declined because Hollins Lettings reference checks are good and Marek has never been a day late
- Accidental damage by tenant: included, £250 excess
- Malicious damage by tenant: included, £500 excess
- Escape of water excess: £400. Higher than the house policy, which still catches me out

## The leak from Flat 5, November 2024

Different from the house claim in every way that matters. Water came from **someone else's flat**, above.

- 18 Nov 2024: Marek rang at 22:10. Water through the bedroom ceiling from Flat 5's dishwasher
- Flat 5 owner: Mrs Okafor, lets through a different agent
- Ceiling, plaster, decorating: **block buildings policy** via the managing agent (Wainwright Estates). Their claim ref WE-BLK-55901, excess £1,000 shared out through service charge next year (my share 1/8 = £125)
- My side: bedroom carpet (2019, £640) and the curtains (£95). Landlord contents claim ref ABL-CL-3318
- Marek's own things (a laptop bag, books, a duvet): **his** contents policy, not mine. He had one, thankfully. Told him so in writing the next morning

## How the claim went

- Loss adjuster: none, under £1,500, handled on photos
- Carpet: agreed £520 (depreciation, 5 years old)
- Curtains: £95
- Less £400 escape of water excess
- **Paid £215**, 6 Dec 2024

Also asked Flat 5's insurer whether they'd cover my excess as the source of the leak. They declined: no negligence shown, a dishwasher hose just fails. Fair enough legally. Annoying.

## Loss of rent, nearly

The bedroom was unusable 18 Nov to 3 Dec while the ceiling dried and was replastered. Marek slept on the sofa bed. Offered him £150 off December's rent, which he accepted. Loss of rent cover only kicks in if the whole flat is uninhabitable, so the £150 came out of my pocket. Tax deductible as reduced rent, see [[Rental income tax]].
